subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native browser-held E2EE chat in core now, define Gateway/plugin APIs first for an external transport, or defer the direction?
rationale: This changes product direction and security boundaries across Gateway protocol, browser UX, routing, transcript storage, key lifecycle, and plugin ownership, so automation cannot safely choose the architecture.

options.title: Design architecture and API seam first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design covering key lifecycle, encrypted envelopes, transcript semantics, relay behavior, and whether a plugin can own the transport.

options.title: Sponsor core-native implementation
options.body: Accept that OpenClaw core owns the browser E2EE transport and require security review plus broad Gateway/UI/protocol tests before code lands.

options.title: Defer to plugin/ClawHub path
options.body: Keep core lean and ask for external delivery only after confirming current or new plugin APIs can support the encrypted browser chat behavior.

recommendation.title: Design architecture and API seam first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned design covering key lifecycle, encrypted envelopes, transcript semantics, relay behavior, and whether a plugin can own the transport.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the earlier keep-open review and has adjacent Gateway/Control UI chat history, making him the best available decision router from the traced owners.
